search_scope: Primary paper pages and author-linked artifacts for D-optimal pairwise or K-way subset design, active ranking, and graph-feedback learning; no generic novelty inference from keyword absence.

closest_prior_work.title: Comparing Few to Rank Many: Active Human Preference Learning Using Randomized Frank-Wolfe Method
overlap: a complete ranking is observed for each selected subset under a Plackett-Luce model
boundary: their paid observation is one human K-way full-ranking interaction over a fixed item universe
our paid unit is one MLE endpoint execution that reveals one scalar grade and deterministically induces preferences only against already executed siblings
our feasible subsets are constrained by generated parent cliques across heterogeneous tasks and physical runs
their target is ranking the same fixed universe; our target is a code critic evaluated on disjoint future physical runs
our study accounts for endpoint cost, dependent clique rank, task/run clustering, noise, leakage, and query/init cost

closest_prior_work.title: Accelerated Experimental Design for Pairwise Comparisons
boundary: does not model one paid endpoint revealing a dependent clique of deterministic sibling comparisons

closest_prior_work.title: Active preference learning for ordering items in- and out-of-sample
boundary: purchases selected pair annotations rather than scalar endpoint executions
does not use the constrained parent-clique observation process of MLE search trees
does not address physical-run disjointness or dependent clique labels derived from one executed vertex

closest_prior_work.title: Sample Complexity Bounds for Active Ranking from Multi-wise Comparisons
overlap: active ranking from winner or full-ranking feedback on multi-item queries
analysis of how multi-wise feedback changes sample complexity
boundary: ranks a fixed item set under a comparison-query budget
does not learn a contextual critic for disjoint future MLE physical runs
does not model endpoint execution as the paid primitive

closest_prior_work.title: Understanding Bandits with Graph Feedback
overlap: one action can reveal structured feedback about multiple alternatives
boundary: online regret with graph feedback is not the frozen offline MLE critic estimand
the present protocol does not claim a new graph-feedback bandit algorithm

forbidden: first K-way or subset-wise active ranking method
first use of item features in active preference learning
algorithmic superiority to DopeWolfe without a matched feedback oracle
claim_restrictions.allowed_if_target522_effect_is_positive: A D-opt-inspired, endpoint-cost-aware instantiation improves run-clean MLE critic label efficiency under the frozen benchmark and audit protocol.
claim_restrictions.allowed_if_only_stage_a_completes: The MLE-specific endpoint-cost and dependent-clique selection protocol is reproducibly instantiated; no efficacy claim.
claim_restrictions.paper_container: Decision Corpus plus Predictor Benchmark plus Audit Protocol; VCCD remains an extension rather than the sole novelty claim.

baseline_rationale.representative_uniform: matched paid endpoint budget and orientation-free topology baseline
baseline_rationale.yield_guarded_breadth: matched MLE-specific topology acquisition baseline already frozen before the candidate
baseline_rationale.vccd: exact centered complete-clique scatter gain for a linear pairwise critic, presented as a domain instantiation rather than a new general D-opt theorem
baseline_rationale.dopewolfe_not_directly_runnable: its oracle purchases one stochastic human full ranking of an arbitrary K-subset from a fixed universe; that is not the endpoint-execution oracle or feasible-set constraint in this benchmark
baseline_rationale.required_discussion: A paper must discuss the ICML 2025 method as closest conceptual prior work and explicitly explain the oracle, feasible-set, target-population, and dependence differences.
